chunks: And al-Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me, saying: Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad informed me, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from a number of our companions [his companions, variant reading], from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Zarif, meaning Ibn Nasih, from Tha'labah ibn Maymun, from 'Abd Allah ibn Yazid, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:
"There is no wudu (ablution) due to pumpkin seeds and small worms; they are only in the position of lice."
(23) As for the report that al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from al-Hasan, his brother, from Zur'ah, from سماعة, who said: I asked him about what invalidates wudu (ablution), and he said:
"The hadath: that you hear its sound or find its smell; and rumbling in the belly, unless it is something you can restrain; and laughing in salat (prayer); and vomiting."

So what this hadith contains regarding laughing and vomiting is to be understood as laughing in which one cannot control himself, and likewise vomiting that causes weakness such that one cannot control himself along with it; and that which indicates this is as follows.

key_terms.اَلدِّيدَانِ: small worms emerging from the body, said not to require wudu (ablution)
key_terms.اَلصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), within which laughter is mentioned
key_terms.اَلْحَدَثُ: ritual occurrence that nullifies purity, especially passing wind here
key_terms.اَلْقَرْقَرَةُ: rumbling in the belly mentioned in connection with possible nullification
key_terms.اَلْقَمْلِ: lice, used as the comparison for insignificant emerging matter
key_terms.اَلْقَيْءُ: vomiting, mentioned as a possible nullifier in a qualified sense
key_terms.اَلْوُضُوءَ: wudu (ablution), the ritual purification discussed in the report

ai.seo_question: What things invalidate wudu (ablution) according to this hadith in Tahdhib al-Ahkam?
ai.summary: This passage addresses rulings on what does and does not invalidate wudu (ablution). It states that the emergence of small worms or similar minor matter does not necessitate wudu (ablution), and it discusses a report on nullifiers of wudu (ablution), with the final line clarifying that laughter and vomiting are meant in severe cases involving loss of control.
